Driving School Basics

Before you can pull over or merge, you need the basics: starting the car, the gas, the brake, reverse. Start the engine first — nothing else works until you do.

Engine off
R
In Context
Your First Time Behind the Wheel
You get in the car and buckle up. First, you start the car (ligar o carro) — the engine turns over and comes to life. You check your mirrors, then step on the gas (acelerar) slowly, feeling the car move forward.

A dog runs into the street, so you step on the brake (pisar no freio) hard and stop just in time. Your instructor asks you to back up (dar ré) into the parking spot behind you.

Halfway there, you forget the clutch and the car stalls (morre / cala) — embarrassing, but it happens to everyone. You restart, finish parking, and finally turn off the car (desligar o carro), proud of your first lesson.
Practice
Put It to Use
Put the steps in order

"Stall" happens by accident in real driving — the engine just dies. It's different from "turn off the car," which you do on purpose.
